canonical_data: A PostgreSQL database of saved articles, ebooks, highlights, notes, tags, and spaced-repetition review state, hosted by the maintainer at lurnby.com by default or run on a self-hosted Postgres and Redis instance from the published install script.
strengths: Purpose-built around spaced repetition and recall practice rather than bolting review onto a generic notes app, so revisiting captured content is a first-class, scheduled workflow rather than a manual habit

Browser extensions capture web articles directly from the reading context, and ebook import covers the other main source of long-form reading, so the two most common capture paths are both native rather than requiring a separate clipper tool
Genuinely self-hostable, with a maintained install script and a conventional Flask, Postgres, and Redis stack, rather than a hosted-only product with source available for reference
weaknesses: No linking, backlinking, or graph view between saved items: organization is tags and categories rather than the networked-notes structure its closer PKM neighbours in this catalog provide
No AI or agent integration of any kind: capture, highlighting, and review are entirely manual

The default and only advertised path is the maintainer's hosted instance; canonical data lives in that hosted Postgres schema rather than portable plain files, and self-hosting requires operating your own database and cache rather than reading files off disk

The default branch has not been touched since January 2026; the only more recent activity is an unmerged frontend-rewrite branch from May 2026, so the shipped open-source tree is quieter than the still-live hosted product
why_it_matters: A working example of memory-science technique, spaced repetition and recall practice, applied to ordinary reading rather than flashcard decks, published as a genuinely self-hostable product rather than a closed reading app.
